synopsis: RadaRays, published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters in 2025, is a real-time radar ray tracer tested with a Navtech CIR radar on a wheel loader in a hall; the booklet identifies this as its most directly relevant heavy-machine radar evidence [f4531, f4532, f15952]. Material-aware reflection modelling substantially improved synthetic-image agreement over a lidar-like model, but the hall required hand-built geometry and tuned materials, and some real double reflections remained missing [f4531, f4824, f4716, f4717, f4962]. Improved image similarity did not deliver a comparable odometry improvement, and an R-CNN trained on real RADIATE data missed most cars in simulated images, partly because target material properties had to be guessed [f5082, f4747, f4855]. These results support evaluating fidelity against the intended downstream function rather than treating image similarity as sufficient evidence of detection or closed-loop intervention performance [f5083, f5084]. Runtime was 7.8–18.8 ms per polar image on an RTX 2070 Super versus 25.8–78.5 ms on a Ryzen 7 3800X CPU over 80,000–400,000 initial rays, limited to the tested radar, model and scene; automatic mesh reconstruction also introduced scanner-occluding artifacts and meshes too large to clean manually [f4936, f4937, f4963, f4964].
